extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or graduate students in algebraic topology; mathematicians studying cohomology
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions, computational tools, and structural theorems for cohomology of chain complexes and topological spaces (singular/cochain viewpoint), including the Universal Coefficient Theorem, Ext computation, long exact sequences, naturality, and standard properties (homotopy invariance, excision, reduced/relative groups).

rubrics_metrics.name: cochain group definition
rubrics_metrics.description: C^n(X; G) = Hom(C_n(X), G), equivalently the group of functions from singular n-simplices of X to the coefficient group G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since singular n-simplices form a basis for C_n(X), values of an n-cochain on simplices can be chosen arbitrarily; thinking of cochains as functions is often the simplest viewpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: coboundary operator and δδ = 0
rubrics_metrics.description: The coboundary δ: C^n(X; G) → C^{n+1}(X; G) is the dual (∂^*) of the chain boundary ∂ and satisfies δϕ = ϕ ∂ for ϕ ∈ Hom(C_n, G); in particular δ∘δ = 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formula: δϕ(σ) = Σ_i (-1)^i ϕ(σ|[v0,...,v̂i,...,vn+1]) for a singular (n+1)-simplex σ. The formal reason δ^2 = 0 is that it is dual to ∂^2 = 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: cohomology group definition
rubrics_metrics.description: H^n(X; G) is defined as Ker δ / Im δ at C^n(X; G), i.e., cocycles modulo coboundaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cocycles are cochains vanishing on boundaries; coboundaries are images of lower-degree cochains under δ.

rubrics_metrics.name: universal coefficient theorem (cohomology)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a chain complex C of free abelian groups, there is a split short exact sequence 0 → Ext(H_{n-1}(C), G) → H^n(C; G) → Hom(H_n(C), G) → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes how cohomology with coefficients in G is algebraically determined by the homology groups H_n(C) and H_{n-1}(C). The sequence splits but the splitting is not natural in general.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ext characterizes the 'extra' part of cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: The term Ker h (or equivalently Coker i^* in the proof) is identified with Ext(H_{n-1}(C), G), the group depending only on H_{n-1}(C) and G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ext can be computed via free resolutions; for finitely generated H it captures torsion contributions shifted up one degree in cohomology.

rubrics_metrics.name: properties of Ext for computations
rubrics_metrics.description: Key properties: Ext(H ⊕ H', G) ≅ Ext(H, G) ⊕ Ext(H', G); Ext(H, G) = 0 if H is free; Ext(Z_n, G) ≅ G / nG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to compute Ext for finitely generated groups by splitting into free part and finite cyclic summands.

rubrics_metrics.name: cohomology with Z coefficients for finitely generated homology
rubrics_metrics.description: If H_n and H_{n-1} are finitely generated with torsion subgroups T_n and T_{n-1}, then H^n(C; Z) ≅ (H_n / T_n) ⊕ T_{n-1}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hom(H_n, Z) picks out the free part of H_n; Ext gives the torsion from H_{n-1}.

rubrics_metrics.name: field coefficients simplify cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: If coefficients are in a field F (or more generally over a PID where modules are free), the Ext term vanishes and H^n(X; F) ≅ Hom_F(H_n(X; F), F).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: With field coefficients cohomology is the exact dual of homology; this is especially simple for F = Z_p or Q.

rubrics_metrics.name: H^0 identification
rubrics_metrics.description: H^0(X; G) ≅ Hom(H_0(X), G); concretely H^0(X; G) consists of functions X → G constant on path-components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, C^0(X;G) are arbitrary functions on points; being a cocycle forces constancy on components.

rubrics_metrics.name: H^1 identification and relation to π1
rubrics_metrics.description: Since Ext(H_0(X), G) = 0, H^1(X; G) ≅ Hom(H_1(X), G). If X is path-connected, Hom(H_1(X), G) ≅ Hom(π1(X)^{ab}, G) and thus can be identified with Hom(π1(X), G) when G is abelian.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In low degrees the universal coefficient theorem often yields direct identifications without Ext complications.

rubrics_metrics.name: duality between boundary and coboundary (δ = ∂^*)
rubrics_metrics.description: For cochains ϕ: C_n → G, δϕ = ϕ ∂; algebraically δ is the dual map to ∂, reversing arrows and satisfying (αβ)^* = β^* α^*.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This linear-algebraic viewpoint explains why cohomology is obtained by applying Hom(−, G) to a chain complex.

rubrics_metrics.name: long exact sequence of a pair (cohomology)
rubrics_metrics.description: From the short exact sequence of cochain complexes 0 ← C^*(A; G) ← C^*(X; G) ← C^*(X, A; G) ← 0 one gets the long exact sequence ... → H^n(X, A; G) → H^n(X; G) → H^n(A; G) → H^{n+1}(X, A; G) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relative cochains are cochains vanishing on simplices in A; the connecting homomorphism δ in cohomology is dual to the homology connecting map.

rubrics_metrics.name: relative cochains exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: There is an exact sequence 0 ← C^n(A; G) ← C^n(X; G) ← C^n(X, A; G) ← 0 where C^n(X,A;G) = Hom(C_n(X)/C_n(A), G), so relative cohomology is computed from cochains vanishing on A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every function on simplices in A extends to X (e.g., by assigning 0 outside A), which gives surjectivity of the restriction map.

rubrics_metrics.name: naturality of universal coefficient sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The short exact sequences in the universal coefficient theorem are natural: a chain map inducing maps on homology induces the corresponding maps on the Ext/Hom sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, the splitting of the sequence is not natural (depends on choices like projections C_n → Z_n).

rubrics_metrics.name: induced isomorphism on cohomology from homology isomorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: If a chain map between chain complexes of free abelian groups induces an isomorphism on homology groups, then it induces an isomorphism on cohomology groups with any coefficient group G (Corollary 3.4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follows from naturality plus the five-lemma applied to the universal coefficient short exact sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: homotopy invariance of cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: If f ≃ g : (X, A) → (Y, B) then f^* = g^* on H^n(Y, B; G); homotopic maps induce the same map on cohomology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof dualizes the homology chain-homotopy argument: a chain homotopy P satisfying g_♯ − f_♯ = ∂P + P∂ yields P^* giving g^♯ − f^♯ = P^* δ + δ P^*.

rubrics_metrics.name: excision in cohomology
rubrics_metrics.description: If Z ⊂ A ⊂ X with cl(Z) ⊂ int(A), then inclusion i: (X − Z, A − Z) → (X, A) induces isomorphisms i^* : H^n(X, A; G) → H^n(X − Z, A − Z; G) for all n.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be proved either by dualizing the homology excision argument or via naturality of the universal coefficient theorem together with the five-lemma.

rubrics_metrics.name: reduced cohomology and difference at degree 0
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduced cohomology groups 9H^n(X; G) relate to unreduced by 9H^n(X; G) = H^n(X; G) for n > 0; the difference at n=0 is accounted for by constant functions coming from the augmentation map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The dual of the augmentation ε: C_0(X) → Z is ε^*: Hom(Z, G) → C^0(X; G) giving the constant functions; reduced cohomology mod out these constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: cohomology classes as obstructions (local vs global)
rubrics_metrics.description: Given ψ ∈ C^1 with δψ = 0, δψ measures the local obstruction to finding ϕ with ψ = δϕ; the cohomology class of ψ is the global obstruction to solving ψ = δϕ (analogy with vanishing curl and line integrals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Geometric interpretations: for G = Z_2 or Z on surfaces, cocycles correspond to transverse curve systems C_ψ and solvability ψ = δϕ corresponds to these curves separating the surface appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: H^1 of graphs and trees computation
rubrics_metrics.description: For a 1-dimensional complex X: H^1(X; G) is a direct product of copies of G, one for each edge of X not in a chosen maximal tree; for a tree H^1(X; G) = 0 because δϕ = ψ is always solvable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contrast with homology: H_1(X; G) is a direct sum (one factor per non-tree edge); the cohomology direct product arises because cochains assign arbitrary values to non-tree edges while cochains on trees are determined by values at a basepoint.
